title: SLO staleness detection and safe rebaseline runbook
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview:
This runbook defines the operational procedure and automation patterns we use to detect SLO staleness, validate whether a rebaseline (redefinition of SLO targets or error budget sizing) is required, and execute a controlled, auditable rebaseline with stakeholder signoff. The goal is to avoid drift between customer-facing expectations and measurable system behavior while preserving reliability and capacity commitments.

Why this matters:
- SLOs degrade in fidelity over time due to workload changes, model rollouts (inference-specific), quantization changes, and new multi-tenant patterns.
- Unchecked rebaselining can hide systemic regressions. This runbook balances signal-driven rebaseline with safeguards: evidence collection, impact simulation, and explicit approvals.

Scope:
- Services: model-serving-api, routing-gateway, embedding-indexer, batched-inference-worker.
- Metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, success_rate (HTTP 2xx / application success), token-processing-rate, cold-start-rate, model-fallback-rate.
- Applies to SLOs that are: availability, latency, and correctness (quality regressions tracked in quality SLOs).

Definitions:
- SLO staleness: a sustained divergence (> 90 days) between observed metric baseline and the SLO's assumed baseline used at last signoff.
- Rebaseline: adjusting the SLO target or error budget window (e.g., 99.9% -> 99.7% for p99) or changing the measurement window (30d -> 14d).

Automated detection signals (first-line):
1) Drift detector job (runs daily): compares rolling 30d metric distribution to the distribution at last SLO signoff. Triggers if: KS-test p-value < 0.01 for p95 latency OR median shifts > 20% OR error budget consumption acceleration > 2x expected.
2) Business signal: sustained increase in customer-impacting alerts (customer tickets labeled slo-impact >= 3) for 7d.
3) Model-change signal: model-version rollout > 10% of traffic or quantized-model variant introduced (from model-onboarding CI).

Alerting and initial triage:
- Alert name: slo-staleness-detected/<<service>>. Severity: P3. Channel: #sre-slo-notifications and an automated ticket in JIRA (component=SRE-SLO).
- Triage owner: service SLO steward. If no steward assigned within 4 hours, paging goes to oncall.

Triage checklist (manual steps):
1) Verify the detector output: download detector artifacts from /var/slo-detector/artifacts/<<id>> (or S3 URI in alert).
2) Confirm dataset windows: 30d observed vs signed baseline snapshot (metadata shows signoff date and commit id).
3) Run lightweight reproducibility checks:
   a) Run synthetic canary (see Synthetic Canary section below) for 30 minutes at current traffic profile.
   b) Run traffic shadowing of 5% of traffic for new model variants if model signal present.
4) If canary/shadow shows no regression, label alert as false-positive and close with notes.

When to consider rebaseline (decision matrix):
- Rebaseline recommended if any of the following hold for at least two independent signals over a 14d sliding window:
  * Mean p95 latency increased > 25% AND customer-facing latency degradations in top 3 tenants.
  * Error budget burn rate sustained > 1.5x and projected depletion < 14 days without configuration change.
  * Production rollout (model or inference-config) has permanently shifted request characteristics (median tokens/request > 30% change) AND mitigations (caching/batching) cannot recover unit economics.
- Rebaseline NOT recommended if there is a short-lived spike (<72 hours) attributable to a deployable/rollbackable root cause (e.g., infra incident).

Evidence collection (required artifacts for any rebaseline):
- Telemetry dump: 30d window of raw request traces (sampled at 1:1000) and full aggregations p50/p95/p99 per tenant.
- Synthetic canary run logs and results JSON.
- Model rollout metadata: versions, quantization profile, kernel variants used per host.
- Cost delta simulation: estimated tokens/host-hour and projected monthly cost with current workload.
- Customer impact evidence: sample of >3 customer tickets and tenant SLA exposure summary.
- Runbook audit: who initiated detector, who triaged, instrumentation snapshots.

Stakeholder signoff workflow (structured approvals):
1) SLO steward prepares a rebaseline proposal PR in the SLO registry repo with: rationale, evidence links, proposed new SLO statement, new measurement window, and rollback criteria. Use template: repo://slo-registry/proposals/rebaseline-<<service>>-<<date>>.md
2) Required reviewers: product-owner, infra-performance lead, finance rep (cost impact), security (if privacy or collection changes), and SRE manager.
3) Approval gates: at least 3 approvers including SRE manager and product-owner. Approvals logged as GitHub PR reviews and mirrored to JIRA ticket.
4) Post-approval: a formal announcement on #slo-changes with links to PR, JIRA, and telemetry snapshots.

Safe rollout steps for approved rebaseline:
1) Update measurement pipeline: add the new SLO target to the metrics collection (Grafana/LokI/SLO-exporter). Deploy configs as a canary to the metrics pipeline.
2) Shadow reporting: enable new SLO target as shadow (no customer-facing effect) for a 7d observation window.
3) Run stress simulations: automated load test that reproduces current traffic at +25% headroom against the new baseline (runbook automation triggers this in the performance lab).
4) If shadow results match projections, schedule rebaseline to become active at the start of a billing cycle or agreed change window (low-traffic weekday).
5) If regressions appear, file RFC to revisit instrumentation or invest in targeted remediation (caching, autoscale, model micro-optimizations).

Rollback and remediation criteria (post-activation):
- Rollback to previous SLO if: customer-impacting incident rate increases by >30% vs baseline within 14 days OR error budget consumption accelerates such that remaining budget < 25%.
- Remediation path: create an incident (SEV3/SEV2 depending on impact), run post-incident evidence capture, and track remediation tickets in SLO project board.

Synthetic Canary (how-to - quick commands):
- Start canary (30m):
  $ slo-canary run --service model-serving-api --profile standard-traffic --duration 30m --output ./canary-results.json
- Summary command:
  $ slo-canary summarize ./canary-results.json --metrics p50,p95,p99,err_rate --compare-to /slo-snapshots/signed-2024-11-01.json

Evidence JSON example (stored alongside proposal):
{
  "id": "rb-2026-01-15-model-serving-api",
  "signoff_snapshot": "git://slo-registry@sha:abc123",
  "observed_windows": "2025-12-15..2026-01-14",
  "p95_change_percent": "+34",
  "error_budget_runrate": "2.1x"
}

Operational tooling integrations:
- Detector job: /ops/slo-detector (Kubernetes CronJob) writes alerts to Alertmanager and artifacts to S3 at s3://redwood-slo-artifacts/<<id>>.
- Canary tooling: slo-canary CLI and perf-lab orchestration.
- PR tracking: SLO registry (git-backed) for proposals and signoffs.
- JIRA template: SRE-SLO-REBASELINE with required checklist fields (automatically populated by detector bot).

Ownership and SLAs for this workflow:
- Detection maintenance: telemetry team (owner: Marco Chen) - 2 business day SLA for fixing false positives in detector.
- Triage and evidence: service SLO steward - 4 hour initial response during business hours.
- Approval quorum: product and SRE manager must respond within 7 business days or escalation to Director of Engineering.

Post-rebaseline review (30/90/180d):
- 30d: Measure real-world impact, publish a short findings note (template: /slo-registry/reviews/30d-<<id>>.md).
- 90d: Cross-team retrospective: include product, finance, ML infra to capture lessons and ROI.
- 180d: Consider merging rebaseline changes into SLO standards if similar patterns repeat across multiple services.

Appendix: Example SLO proposal summary (text to include in PR body):
- Current SLO: model-serving-api latency p95 < 200ms (30d window).
- Observed baseline: p95 = 270ms (30d window), p99 = 520ms.
- Proposal: change p95 target to 250ms and move measurement window to 14d for detection sensitivity; keep p99 target unchanged and introduce a secondary latency SLO for top-5 tenants.
- Rationale: sustained workload token-size increase (+38%) from new LLM-4-1536 rollout and cache miss rate increase due to sharded KV upgrade.
- Rollout plan: shadow 7d -> stress test -> activate at next billing cycle -> monitor 14d.
